text: Name a movie about AI or robots
note: Feature films, animated films and documentaries where an AI or robot is central. Sequels count separately

answers.q: 1970: a US defense AI links up with its Soviet twin and takes charge of the planet. Alignment cinema, decades early.
HAL gets a second chance, and an apology.
1986. Mall security robots, a lightning storm, a lot of teenagers.
Disney, 1979. V.I.N.CENT is cute; Maximilian is a spinning-blade nightmare.
1953. A man in a gorilla suit and a diving helmet. Often listed among the worst films ever made.
Al Pacino invents an AI actress, and the whole world falls for her.
Nine shorts. 'The Second Renaissance' explains how the war with the machines started.

answers.a: Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya

answers.q: Woody Allen, 1973, hiding from a future police state disguised as a robot butler.
A comedy in which an AI picks James Corden's voice and decides humanity's fate by studying Melissa McCarthy.

answers.a: We Need to Talk About AI

answers.q: A German scientist trials a humanoid robot built to be her perfect partner.
Disney Channel, 1999. The house AI turns into an overbearing mom and locks the family in.

answers.a: The Day the Earth Stood Still
answers.q: 1951. Klaatu barada nikto, or Gort gets cross.
1956. Robby the Robot's debut, and The Tempest in space.
Ryan Reynolds as a game NPC who becomes self-aware.
Giant robots punching giant monsters, piloted through a two-person mind-meld called the Drift.
Spelled that way on purpose. Nobody knows why.
Daft Punk scored it and made a cameo in their helmets.
1984. A computer falls for its owner's neighbour after he spills champagne on it.
1977. An AI traps a woman in her smart house. Peak 70s.
A retired jewel thief teaches his care robot to pick locks.
Colin Farrell's family android breaks down; the memories it kept are the film.
1998. Military-grade AI chips in action figures. What could go wrong?
Tom Hanks builds a robot to look after his dog after the apocalypse.
A dog and his robot in 1980s New York. No dialogue, Oscar-nominated, devastating.
Joy Buolamwini discovers face recognition can't see her face until she wears a white mask.
The 2024 documentary on Demis Hassabis and DeepMind, by the AlphaGo film's director.
John Carpenter's 1974 debut. The crew has to talk a sentient bomb out of exploding.
Rajinikanth vs Rajinikanth's robot double. One of India's most expensive films at the time.
Kubrick developed it for years; Spielberg made it in 2001.
Pixar, 2008. Barely a word of dialogue in the first 40 minutes.
Verhoeven, 1987. Dead cop, cyborg cop, satire on a budget.
1983. A teenager almost starts WW3 with a modem. Shall we play a game?
Brad Bird, 1999. 'You are who you choose to be.'
Johnny Depp uploads himself, and the internet gets weird.
Michael Crichton, 1973. A malfunctioning theme-park robot hunts tourists. Jurassic Park, but with Yul Brynner.
Mamoru Oshii, 1995. The Wachowskis showed it to producers to pitch The Matrix.
1982. One of the first films with extensive computer animation, and Disney was nervous.
Mostly about codebreaking, but the title is Turing's name for his test.
Fritz Lang, 1927. The Maschinenmensch set the template for every movie robot after.
The 2017 documentary on Lee Sedol vs DeepMind. Move 37 gets its own drumroll.
1984. Cameron's budget was about $6.4M, and Arnold has 17 lines.
1999. Humans as batteries, at least in the final script. Bullet time forever.
Kubrick, 1968. HAL is the most human character in the film.
Alex Garland, 2015. A Turing test that ends with the tester locked in.
Spike Jonze, 2013. Set in a near-future that arrived early.
Ridley Scott, 1982. Based on Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? Seven versions and counting.
2004. Asimov's Three Laws, Will Smith's Converse.
